subject: Post-call recap: HealthSpring model shortlist + quantization trade plan
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@healthspring.ai>; HealthSpring IT <it@healthspring.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: model shortlist + perf/quality trade plan

Hi Olivia — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed plan so we have the same storming board: 

Key asks you called out:
- Target latency: P95 < 350ms for ~128 token responses (conversational routing)
- Cost target: ~<$0.015 / 1k tokens (goal)
- Strong preference to minimize hallucination on clinical notes summarization

Model shortlist (recommended for evaluation):
1) Mistral-Instruct-7B — best cost/latency balance for short responses (baseline)
2) Mixtral-8x7B — our recommended throughput winner for quantization (higher ops efficiency)
3) Redwood-13B-v1 — higher-quality option if latency budget allows (better instruction fidelity)

Quantization and tuning notes (high-level):
- AWQ (4-bit) yields biggest throughput uplift with modest quality drop on some instruction tasks; good candidate to meet your latency/cost targets.
- GPTQ (4-bit) is a middle ground: slightly less throughput but better retention of instruction-following quality.
- FP8 (upcoming) preserves quality best but requires newer infra and careful stability testing.

Attachments I uploaded: healthspring-quant-benchmarks-20261124.csv, prompt-sets-healthspring-v1.jsonl (sample prompts from your call and our probe set).

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood runs a focused eval across the three models + AWQ/GPTQ on your seed prompts (we use the prompt set attached). [Lauren / Jordan to drive]
2) We share per-model P95 latency and cost estimates plus a short quality delta table (BLEU/ROUGE-like / hallucination metrics). [Jordan] 
3) Sign off on SLOs and whether you want us to prototype AWQ tuning on Mixtral 8x7b (we recommend one week of tuning). [Customer decision] 
4) Security ask: if you want us to run on a private deployment (VPC), confirm SOC2 contacts and required evidence to proceed.

Can you confirm the latency / cost targets above and whether we have permission to run AWQ tuning on a sample of your prompts? If yes, we’ll kick off the eval and share initial numbers within 48 hours.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

---
Attachments: healthspring-quant-benchmarks-20261124.csv (csv), prompt-sets-healthspring-v1.jsonl (jsonl)

From: Olivia Chen <olivia@healthspring.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthSpring IT <it@healthspring.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model shortlist + perf/quality trade plan

Thanks Lauren — appreciate the clear recap. Confirming our targets: P95 < 350ms for 128 tokens and cost target under $0.015/1k tokens.

Couple clarifications before you start tuning:
- Hallucination sensitivity: our internal metric flags anything that invents patient medication details; that rate must not increase by more than 0.5 percentage points versus our current baseline.
- Can you include a small synthetic test set with edge-case prompts (we attached HS_eval_seed.csv) and run the full pipeline against it?
- Please include our security contact on any uploads: sec-contact@healthspring.ai — they will request SOC2 evidence and a list of where logs are stored.

If AWQ tuning gives you quick wins on Mixtral, go ahead — we authorize the initial week of tuning on the evaluation bucket only.

Olivia
Product Lead, HealthSpring
olivia@healthspring.ai

---
Attachment: HS_eval_seed.csv (csv)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@healthspring.ai>, HealthSpring IT <it@healthspring.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model shortlist + perf/quality trade plan

Hi Olivia — thanks, noted on the hallucination budget and security contact (sec-contact@healthspring.ai). We kicked off a short trade study this morning; summary highlights below (high-level, preliminary):

Quantization trade summary (Mixtral-8x7b / 128-token conversational workload):
- Baseline (FP16): P95 ~ 920ms; throughput ~ 65 qps per GPU; baseline rouge-like metric = 0.72; hallucination rate = 2.1%
- GPTQ 4-bit: P95 ~ 360ms (2.5x throughput uplift); rouge delta = -1.2 pts (0.71); hallucination = 2.5% (up +0.4)
- AWQ 4-bit: P95 ~ 330ms (2.8x uplift); rouge delta = -2.6 pts (0.697); hallucination = 2.8% (up +0.7)
- FP8 (experimental infra): P95 ~ 780ms; rouge delta = -0.4 pts (0.716); hallucination = 2.2%

Interpretation:
- AWQ is the fastest route to meet your latency/cost targets but shows a measurable drop on our summarization proxy and a slightly higher hallucination delta (just above your 0.5pp tolerance).
- GPTQ trades a bit more latency for better quality retention; still close to your P95 target.
- FP8 preserves quality best but doesn’t help latency enough on current infra (requires upgraded kernels/hardware).

Artifacts uploaded: quant-tradeoffs-summary-20261125.pdf, detailed CSVs and the prompt set (links below). We will also push run logs to the S3 eval bucket and flag any seeds that cause nondeterministic variance.

Proposed tactical path (recommended):
1) Short-list Mixtral + GPTQ as the primary production candidate if you need strict fidelity; AWQ as the aggressive cost/latency option behind a canary/fallback.
2) We run an AWQ prototype on a constrained eval cluster (one week, per your approval) and measure hallucination on the HS_eval_seed set.
3) If AWQ exceeds your hallucination delta, we can either: (a) fall back to GPTQ for production, or (b) tune decoding parameters (top-p/temp/penalties) and apply KV-prefix caching to reduce token budget.

Owners / immediate next steps:
- Ben: spin up AWQ tuning job for Mixtral-8x7b and push logs to s3.redwood-internal/healthspring/logs/awq/ (Ben to own).
- Lauren: coordinate SOC2 evidence handoff to sec-contact@healthspring.ai and confirm where we can store the artifacts (S3 vs VPC).
- Jordan: schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive early next week to go over the tradeoffs and tuning knobs.

Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com

---
Attachments: quant-tradeoffs-summary-20261125.pdf (pdf)
Related links: https://s3.redwood-internal/healthspring/benchmarks/20261124/

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model shortlist + perf/quality trade plan

Quick update — I kicked off AWQ tuning on Mixtral-8x7b this morning against the HS_eval_seed set. First observations: P95 ~ 310ms for 128 tokens on the eval instance after the initial tuning pass (meets target), cost projection looks promising (est. $0.012/1k tokens).

Flag for the team: I’m seeing some deterministic decoding drift versus baseline that causes ~0.8-1.5 pt rouge variance depending on seed. I will capture exact seeds and push them into the logs folder. If we see hallucination delta > 0.5pp on your clinical edge cases we should either tighten decoding params or switch to GPTQ for that route.

I’ll push a short report to the S3 link and ping sec-contact@healthspring.ai once artifacts are available.

—Ben
Ben Carter
SRE / Performance Tuning | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
